# gcore_waap_domain_advanced_rules (Data Source)

Advanced rules are CEL-expression WAAP rules that allow, block, challenge, monitor or tag requests to a domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gcore_waap_domain_advanced_rules" "example_waap_domain_advanced_rules" {
  domain_id = 1
  action = "block"
  description = "This rule blocks all the requests coming form a specific IP address"
  enabled = false
  name = "Block by specific IP rule"
  ordering = "-id"
  phase = "access"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (Number) The domain ID

### Optional

- `action` (String) Filter to refine results by specific actions
Available values: "allow", "block", "captcha", "handshake", "monitor", "tag".
- `description` (String) Filter rules based on their description. Supports '*' as a wildcard character.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Filter rules based on their active status
- `max_items` (Number) Max items to fetch, default: 1000
- `name` (String) Filter rules based on their name. Supports '*' as a wildcard character.
- `ordering` (String) Determine the field to order results by
Available values: "id", "name", "description", "enabled", "action", "phase", "-id", "-name", "-description", "-enabled", "-action", "-phase".
- `phase` (String) Filter rules based on the WAAP request/response phase for applying the rule.


The "access" phase is responsible for modifying the request before it is sent to the origin server. 

The "header_filter" phase is responsible for modifying the HTTP headers of a response before they are sent back to the client.

The "body_filter" phase is responsible for modifying the body of a response before it is sent back to the client.
Available values: "access", "header_filter", "body_filter".

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) The items returned by the data source (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `action` (Attributes) The action that the rule takes when triggered. Only one action can be set per rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--action))
- `description` (String) The description assigned to the rule
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether or not the rule is enabled
- `id` (Number) The unique identifier for the rule
- `name` (String) The name assigned to the rule
- `phase` (String) The WAAP request/response phase for applying the rule. Default is "access".


The "access" phase is responsible for modifying the request before it is sent to the origin server. 

The "header_filter" phase is responsible for modifying the HTTP headers of a response before they are sent back to the client.

The "body_filter" phase is responsible for modifying the body of a response before it is sent back to the client.
Available values: "access", "header_filter", "body_filter".
- `source` (String) A CEL syntax expression that contains the rule's conditions. Allowed objects are: request, whois, session, response, tags, `user_defined_tags`, `user_agent`, `client_data`.

More info can be found here: https://gcore.com/docs/waap/waap-rules/advanced-rules

<a id="nestedatt--items--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.action`

Read-Only:

- `allow` (Map of String) The WAAP allows the request
- `block` (Attributes) WAAP block action behavior could be configured with response status code and action duration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--action--block))
- `captcha` (Map of String) The WAAP presents the user with a captcha
- `handshake` (Map of String) The WAAP performs automatic browser validation
- `monitor` (Map of String) The WAAP monitors the request but takes no action
- `tag` (Attributes) WAAP tag action gets a list of tags to tag the request scope with (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--action--tag))

<a id="nestedatt--items--action--block"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.action.block`

Read-Only:

- `action_duration` (String) How long a rule's block action will apply to subsequent requests. Can be specified in seconds or by using a numeral followed by 's', 'm', 'h', or 'd' to represent time format (seconds, minutes, hours, or days). Empty time intervals are not allowed.
- `status_code` (Number) A custom HTTP status code that the WAAP returns if a rule blocks a request
Available values: 403, 405, 418, 429.


<a id="nestedatt--items--action--tag"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.action.tag`

Read-Only:

- `tags` (List of String) The list of user defined tags to tag the request with
